description: Side-by-side compilation of two Washington Post opinion headlines by columnist Max Boot, joined by the caption '... when previously' to suggest a contradiction. The top headline (December 19) criticizes Trump's Syria pullout as 'a giant Christmas gift to our enemies'; the bottom (April 19) reads 'Trump can't do anything right - We don't need troops in Syria'.
text: The Washington Post. Democracy Dies in Darkness. Opinions. Trump's surprise Syria pullout is a giant Christmas gift to our enemies. By Max Boot. Columnist. December 19 at 2:53 PM. ... when previously. Global Opinions. Trump can't do anything right - We don't need troops in Syria. By Max Boot. Columnist. April 19.
flags: The '... when previously' caption is an added editorial framing implying hypocrisy; the second headline's phrasing may be paraphrased or altered from the original column title

description: Two-column comparison meme equating the 1930s German Antifaschistische Aktion with modern Antifa. Left column, captioned '1933 Paramilitary Wing of The Communist Party of Germany', shows the red Antifaschistische Aktion two-flag logo and black-and-white photos of large KPD-era rallies with antifascist banners. Right column, captioned '2017 Paramilitary Wing of The Democratic Party of America', shows the modern black/red Antifascist Action logo, a photo of a masked black-clad group posing with flags and sticks, and Antifa stickers including one reading 'Nationalists Not Welcome'.
text: 1933 Paramilitary Wing of The Communist Party of Germany. 2017 Paramilitary Wing of The Democratic Party of America. ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION. ANTIFASCIST ACTION. ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION. ES LEBE DIE ROTE EINHEITSFRONT. DAS ABZEICHEN DES ANTIFASCHISTEN. NATIONALISTS NOT WELCOME. ANTIFASCIST ACTION. SUPPORT YOUR LOCAL ANTIFA. A.C.A.B.
flags: The captions' claims that Antifa is the 'paramilitary wing' of the KPD or of the Democratic Party are the meme's assertions, not established fact
Individuals in the modern group photo are masked private individuals and are not identified

description: Collage of three captioned archival photographs showing Donald Trump socializing with prominent Black public figures. Left: a 1997 photo captioned as Rev. Al Sharpton leaning to talk to Rev. Jesse Jackson as Jackson shakes hands with Trump at the launch of the Rainbow Coalition's Wall Street Project. Top right: an uncaptioned event photo of Trump talking with a group of men including Jesse Jackson and a man resembling James Brown. Bottom right: a Ron Galella/WireImage photo captioned as Don King, Donald Trump, Jesse Jackson and John H. Johnson surrounded by security detail on June 27, 1988.
text: The Rev. Al Sharpton leans to talk to the Rev. Jesse Jackson as he shakes hands with Donald Trump during launching of the Rainbow Coalition's Wall Street Project at the World Trade Center Marriot Marquis in 1997. PREV. 24 of 26. Photo Credit: WireImage / Ron Galella, Ltd. Don King, Donald Trump, Jesse Jackson and John H. Johnson are surrounded by security detail on June 27, 1988.
flags: The man in sunglasses in the top-right photo resembles James Brown but is not named by any caption; identification uncertain
Captions are as printed in the source screenshots; the caption's venue name 'World Trade Center Marriot Marquis' appears as written

description: Close-up photograph, framed as a phone screenshot with black bars, of a stainless-steel IWC wristwatch with a white dial, blue hands, two sub-dials and a brown leather strap, lying on a black textured folio or notebook next to a black-and-silver ballpoint pen on a light wooden desk. The watch dial bears the IWC logo and is consistent with an IWC Portugieser chronograph; the pen is consistent with a Montblanc StarWalker-style pen. This is one of the 'watch and pen' desk photos posted in the Q drops, where the watch's displayed time was treated as a signal by followers.
flags: Watch model and pen brand identified from appearance only — consistent with IWC Portugieser chronograph and a Montblanc-style pen, not certain
The exact time shown on the dial is difficult to read precisely at this angle
